title: Dynamic Tail Trimming & KV Lifecycle — Initiative Tracker for Thrifty Serving
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Reduce per-request token cost by combining dynamic tail-trimming (adaptive generation length caps) with a principled KV cache lifecycle (TTL, eviction, and refresh heuristics) without measurable regression in perceived response quality. We expect a 12–20% average token reduction on long-form completions and a 5–8% reduction in 95th-percentile token spend for chat workloads after rollout.

Scope: 1) Implement a server-side dynamic tail-trimming policy that sets an adaptive max_new_tokens per request based on prompt type, past-session length, and quality signal heuristics (entropy/stop-token heuristics, customer defaults). 2) Introduce KV cache lifecycle controls: per-model TTLs, adaptive hot-key pinning, and a background refresh policy for frequently accessed prefix states. 3) Add monitoring, automated regressions checks against the evaluation corpus, and rollout gates tied to token-savings and quality thresholds.

Success metrics: token-saved-per-request, token-cost-reduction (dollars), quality-regression-rate on eval prompts (target <1.5% severe regressions), latency impact (p50/p95 target no worse than +5% from baseline), and percentage of requests using trimmed tails.

Trade-offs: Aggressive trimming risks truncated outputs hurting UX; longer TTLs reduce compute at cost of potential staleness and memory utilization. We'll mitigate by conservative initial thresholds, canary rollouts, quality fallback to full model when heuristics flag risk, and per-customer opt-out.

Acceptance criteria and rollout plan are below. This is intentionally focused on server-side controls so client SDK changes are minimal (opt-in knobs).

acceptance_criteria: Server-side trimming reduces average tokens-per-request by >=12% in canary vs baseline for targeted workloads
No more than 1.5% severe quality regressions on evaluation set (human-labeled), and automated semantic-similarity regression <3%
P95 latency change <+5% from baseline in canary window
KV cache TTL defaults reduce token cost by >=5% without exceeding memory budget in dedicated pools
Console shows rollout status, per-customer opt-out, and per-route token-savings metrics
Automated rollback triggers implemented (savings threshold and degradation threshold) and tested in staging
risks: User-visible truncation leading to support tickets — mitigated via conservative defaults and per-customer opt-out
Mis-tuned TTLs causing KV store memory pressure on Dedicated clusters — mitigation: memory guardrails and metrics alerts
Quality regressions for niche prompt patterns — mitigation: sentinel prompts and quick rollback path
Interference with function-calling or structured-output flows — mitigation: add explicit opt-out for function calls and run function-call tests in the eval harness
